morgan_support: FYI customer on freemium reported embeddings failing after a small client bump — getting a dimension mismatch error when batching. they said it worked before.
liam_dev: can you paste the raw payload they send? often it's single vs batch encoding or double-stringified JSON.
morgan_support: here's what they pasted: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...

{
  "model": "embed-english-1536",
  "input": "[\"hello\", \"world\"]"
}
```
They said they switched from an in-house wrapper to using fetch direct in a worker. Getting: `400 Bad Request - embedding vector dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1537` when they pass the result to their similarity service.
nora_eng: aha — that's double-stringified. server expects input: array<string> (or array<object {input: string}>). Instead they're sending a single string that contains JSON for an array. That will be processed as one long string (with extra escaping or hidden chars), which can produce different tokenization and sometimes odd downstream dimension interpretation when they later attach or compare vectors. Also watch for BOM (UTF-8 BOM) — I ran into that once where first character added an extra token.
liam_dev: concrete repro steps for support to give to customer: 1) confirm Content-Type is application/json and body is a real JSON array not a string. 2) try this minimal curl which should succeed: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '\n  {"model":"embed-english-1536","input":["hello","world"]}\n  '
```
If that works, compare with their failing payload. If they still get mismatch, dump bytes of first element to check for BOM: 
```python
with open('sample.txt','rb') as f:
    b=f.read()
print(b[:4])  # look for b'\xef\xbb\xbf'
```

morgan_support: customer tried the curl above and it passed. they then ran a quick check and saw their worker was doing `body = await request.text(); JSON.parse(body)` but their wrapper had already done `JSON.stringify([...])` upstream. so double stringify. they also had an old library that inserted a leading `\ufeff` (BOM) when constructing strings from a file. they sent a screenshot of hex: `ef bb bf 22 48 65 6c 6c 6f` which is BOM then quoted string.
nora_eng: recommended fix to send array directly (not string). examples to paste: 
```js
// correct
fetch('/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json','Authorization': `Bearer ${KEY}`},
  body: JSON.stringify({model:'embed-english-1536', input:['hello','world']})
})

// wrong (double-stringify)
const payload = JSON.stringify(['hello','world'])
fetch('/v1/embeddings', {body: JSON.stringify({model:'embed-english-1536', input: payload})})
```
liam_dev: added note for support: also warn about mixing NDJSON or multipart — if they use NDJSON ensure each line is a JSON string/object per docs. Batching via array is simpler for troubleshooting. And if they feed embeddings to a downstream similarity join, ensure you don't accidentally send textual payload where vectors expected (dimension mismatch messages often come from the similarity service not embeddings generation).
infra-bot: deploy-check OK for embed-english-1536, no regressions detected in the last 24h :white_check_mark:
morgan_support: resolved with customer — they removed the double-stringify and stripped BOM at source. customer confirmed stable throughput again. closing but leaving notes here so other agents see the BOM + double-stringify gotcha. :memo:

liam_dev: small doc PR idea: add a short troubleshooting snippet about double-stringify + BOM under embeddings FAQ. I'll draft one this afternoon. :+1:
